sections.html:
The Town of Babylon fronts the Atlantic side of Long Island in Suffolk County. About 78.3% of homes are lived in by their owners, with a typical value of $522,100. Mortgage holders spend close to $3,206 monthly, and a typical rent is $2,168. Residents numbered 219,766 in 2025, across 69,085 households averaging 3.13 people.

Buyers read the tax bill closely at those costs. A lot of the housing went up in the postwar boom, so be ready for questions about how old the roof and furnace are.

sections.h2: Villages, hamlets and what changes between them
sections.html:
Three incorporated villages and a long list of hamlets share the town, so an address can follow different local rules than the town name suggests.

  • Villages: Amityville in the southwest, Lindenhurst in the south and Babylon in the southeast
  • Hamlets: Copiague, Deer Park, East Farmingdale, North Amityville, North Babylon, North Lindenhurst, West Babylon, Wheatley Heights and Wyandanch

Town Hall stands on East Sunrise Highway in Lindenhurst. For a house inside one of the villages, ask the village office what it adds on top of the town's taxes and permits. Tell buyers which Long Island Rail Road station is nearest, because commuters sort listings by it.

sections.h2: Water, flood zones and sewer billing
sections.html:
More than half of the town's 114 square miles is water, and the land averages about 6.6 feet above sea level. That low ground drives insurance costs and buyer questions. Before listing, ask your insurance agent if the house is in a flood zone.

Sewer billing changed on January 1, when all Suffolk County sewer districts merged into the Suffolk County Wastewater Management District. Your rate or the way you are billed may differ now. Read the sewer line on your tax bill, and have the title company verify it before closing.

sections.h2: Tax calendar and late payment costs
sections.html:
The tax year starts December 1 and ends November 30. A single bill goes out around mid-December, payable in full or in two halves. Half one comes due in the second week of January, and half two at the end of May.

What late taxes cost in Babylon
Payment statusAdded cost
First half paid late1% for each month, topping out at 5% in mid to late May
Unpaid after May ends (delinquent, sent to the Suffolk County Comptroller in Riverhead)5% penalty plus 1% monthly interest, counted from February 1
Partial payment at the ComptrollerAccepted starting at $200
Card payment online2.35% fee (e-checks add $1)
Balance still open at the tax lien sale, usually in DecemberCounty sells a lien on the property

The Receiver of Taxes only collects. Budgets from the school district, county and town set the amounts, and the school portion is generally the largest. Not receiving a bill does not excuse a late payment, so ask for a copy if yours never arrived.

sections.h2: How to pay, and who can get a copy of the bill
sections.html:
You can pay online through the payment processor, mail a check with the detached stub, or pay at Town Hall in the main hallway. The counter accepts cash and checks but no cards, and a drop box takes checks during business hours. A mailed payment is credited on its postmark date, though a metered postmark is not accepted.

Owners who are 65 or older, or disabled, in a one, two or three-family house can name a consenting adult to get duplicate bills and unpaid-tax notices. Applications are due October 1. Selling a parent's house? Check whether anyone was ever named, since an unopened bill is how many balances turn delinquent.

Babylon's Department of Assessment takes exemption applications until March 1 and denies late ones. Programs include Enhanced STAR, Aged, Alternative military service, Cold War service, volunteer firefighter and ambulance worker, disability with limited income, Capital Improvement, and a break for first-time buyers of a newly built home. Newcomers to Basic STAR get a state credit in place of a school tax exemption.

Exemptions belong to the person who qualified, not the house. A senior or military exemption on your bill will end with the sale, and the buyer's bill may rise. Say so early.

To dispute an assessment, file Form RP-524 at no cost. The town review boards in Suffolk County meet on the third Tuesday in May, and in 2027 that is May 18. The town builds values from square footage and amenities, so check those details on your record first.

Sellers normally pay New York's transfer tax of $2 per $500 of price. The TP-584 return is filed with the Suffolk County Clerk, with payment due within 15 days after delivery of the deed.

Third-party payers such as banks, title companies and attorneys pay a $1 duplicate tax bill fee, sent as a separate check. Plan for that when a title company clears your open tax bill at closing.

Listing ties you to the buyer's mortgage schedule. A cash buyer accepts the house as is and closes when you are ready, which helps with postponed repairs, a late tax balance or an estate. Whichever you choose, collect the deed, your newest tax statement and a payoff from the lender.

sections.h2: Steps to take before you accept an offer
sections.html:
1. Pull your newest tax bill and confirm both halves are paid.
  2. If the Comptroller holds a balance, request a payoff that adds in the penalty and interest.
  3. List every exemption on the house and warn the buyer which ones will end.
  4. Look up your sewer line and flood zone so the answers are ready when buyers ask.
  5. Learn how the title company plans to clear the open bill and cover the $1 fee at closing.

Also gather any paperwork on past repairs. Buyers near the water ask about basement moisture and storm damage, and a folder of receipts answers them before they turn into price cuts. If you owe a tax balance, a sale can still go forward: the title company pays it from the proceeds, which is why the payoff figure matters before you agree to a price.

These steps barely slow a cash sale. With payoff figures in hand and a clean title search, a cash buyer can set the closing date.

faqs.q: When do Babylon tax payments come due?
faqs.a: One bill goes out in mid-December. You can split it: the first half is due in January and the second at the end of May, and a late first half adds 1% a month.

faqs.q: Where do Babylon taxes go after May 31?
faqs.a: Unpaid balances move to the Suffolk County Comptroller's Office in Riverhead. A 5% penalty applies, along with 1% monthly interest running from February 1.

faqs.q: Does my STAR or senior exemption pass to the buyer in Babylon?
faqs.a: No, the buyer must apply on their own by March 1, and expect a higher bill meanwhile.

faqs.q: Do Babylon sellers owe a transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The state rate is $2 for each $500, and sellers usually pay it. File the TP-584 with the Suffolk County Clerk within 15 days after the deed.

faqs.q: When must a Babylon assessment complaint be filed?
faqs.a: Review boards in Suffolk County's towns sit the third Tuesday of May. Use form RP-524, which is free.
